screening_decisions.reason: Randomised double-blind crossover trial comparing monotherapy with carbamazepine and diphenylhydantoin (phenytoin) in patients with psychomotor (focal onset) epilepsy. Meets population, intervention, comparison, and design criteria.

Randomised trial comparing monotherapy with phenytoin and carbamazepine in newly diagnosed epileptic patients. Although the primary reported outcome is cognitive function, it directly compares the two drugs of interest as monotherapy and may contain relevant time-to-event data for the IPD review.
This is a systematic review and meta-analysis synthesizing individual patient data from multiple trials. It is not a primary randomised controlled trial.

Prospective randomised pragmatic trial comparing monotherapy with four drugs including phenytoin and carbamazepine in adults with newly diagnosed tonic-clonic or partial seizures. Fully meets all selection criteria.
Methodological paper discussing the design and analysis of equivalence trials. Not a primary clinical trial comparing carbamazepine and phenytoin.
Prospective observational cohort study identifying factors associated with refractory epilepsy. Not a randomised controlled trial comparing carbamazepine and phenytoin monotherapy.
Educational review article on principles of antiepileptic drug therapy. Not a primary clinical trial.
Observational study assessing cognitive function in patients starting, withdrawing, or switching antiepileptic drugs. Not a randomised comparative trial of carbamazepine versus phenytoin.
Preclinical animal study (rats) investigating phenytoin-folate interactions. Does not meet population or study design criteria.

Prospective randomised pragmatic trial comparing monotherapy with four drugs including phenytoin and carbamazepine in children with newly diagnosed tonic-clonic or partial seizures. Fully meets all selection criteria.
Epidemiological survey estimating incidence and prevalence of various neurologic disorders. Not a clinical trial.

Controlled study evaluating carbamazepine in institutionalized patients with refractory seizures already on combination therapy. Not a monotherapy randomised trial comparing carbamazepine versus phenytoin.
Epidemiological study assessing incidence rates of epilepsy in HMO populations. Not a clinical trial.

Multi-center double-blind randomised trial comparing monotherapy with four drugs including carbamazepine and phenytoin in adults with partial and secondarily generalized tonic-clonic seizures. Fully meets all selection criteria.
Review article discussing diagnostic accuracy and case ascertainment in epilepsy epidemiology. Not a clinical trial.

Prospective study comparing monotherapy with phenytoin and carbamazepine in patients with newly diagnosed focal epilepsy. Although the primary outcome is neurophysiological (evoked potentials), it directly compares the two drugs of interest as monotherapy and may contain relevant clinical data. Included conservatively.
Population-based prospective incidence study of epilepsy in Iceland. Not a clinical trial.
Methodological paper describing statistical techniques for meta-analysis of time-to-event outcomes. Not a primary clinical trial.
Meta-analysis estimating global prevalence and burden of epilepsy. Not a primary clinical trial.
Position paper and clinical guidelines on epilepsy classification. Not a primary clinical trial.
Double-blind RCT comparing carbamazepine and diphenylhydantoin (phenytoin) as monotherapy in patients with temporal lobe (focal) seizures. Meets all selection criteria.
Review article about phenytoin uses in dermatology, not an RCT comparing CBZ vs PHT monotherapy for epilepsy.
Double-blind crossover RCT comparing carbamazepine and phenytoin as monotherapy in patients with focal and major generalized seizures. Meets all selection criteria.
RCT randomizing patients to CBZ, PHT, or VPA monotherapy. While primary outcome is cognitive, the CBZ vs PHT comparison exists and seizure outcomes may be reported. Conservative inclusion.
In vitro mechanistic study using cell cultures, not a clinical RCT.
Study focuses on zonisamide pharmacokinetics and drug interactions, not an RCT comparing CBZ vs PHT monotherapy.
In vitro mechanistic study using neuroblastoma cells, not a clinical RCT.
Methodological guidelines paper, not a clinical trial.
Multi-drug comparison including phenytoin but NOT carbamazepine. Does not meet the CBZ vs PHT comparison criterion.
Network meta-analysis (secondary analysis of existing trials), not a primary RCT.
Observational case series studying seizure exacerbation, not an RCT comparing CBZ vs PHT.
Systematic review on teratogenicity outcomes, not a primary RCT comparing CBZ vs PHT for seizure outcomes.
Case series reporting aberrant reactions to carbamazepine, not an RCT comparing CBZ vs PHT.

Double-blind crossover RCT comparing CBZ and PHT as sole treatment in patients with partial and generalized epilepsy. Primary outcome is EEG but seizure incidence was also assessed. Conservative inclusion.
Q&A format discussing pregnancy safety, not an RCT.
RCT randomizing patients to CBZ, PHT, or phenobarbitone monotherapy. While primary outcome is cognitive, the CBZ vs PHT comparison exists. Conservative inclusion.
Observational study on trace element concentrations, not an RCT comparing CBZ vs PHT.
Controlled trial of carbamazepine only, no comparison with phenytoin.

Prospective trials comparing phenytoin and carbamazepine monotherapy in patients with grand mal or partial seizures. Design unclear from abstract (may be non-randomized). Conservative inclusion pending full-text review.
Observational study on congenital malformations, not an RCT comparing CBZ vs PHT for seizure outcomes.

This is a double-blind crossover study comparing carbamazepine (CBZ) with diphenylhydantoin (DPH/phenytoin). The abstract describes 20 patients completing the protocol with seizure outcomes reported for both drugs. While the exact seizure types are not explicitly stated, this appears to be a randomized controlled trial comparing the two drugs of interest. Conservative approach warrants inclusion.

This is a systematic review assessing neurodevelopmental outcomes in children following prenatal exposure to AEDs. It does not compare carbamazepine vs phenytoin monotherapy, nor does it focus on seizure control outcomes. Wrong outcome focus and study type.
This is a methodological paper discussing IPD meta-analysis approaches in AED research. It is not a primary randomized controlled trial comparing carbamazepine vs phenytoin monotherapy.

This is an observational prospective registry study examining congenital malformation risks from AED exposure during pregnancy. It is not a randomized controlled trial comparing carbamazepine vs phenytoin monotherapy for seizure control.
This is a methodological paper about meta-analysis techniques (likely about I² statistic). It is not a primary clinical trial comparing carbamazepine vs phenytoin.
This is a methodological study examining outcome reporting bias across Cochrane reviews. It is not a primary randomized controlled trial comparing carbamazepine vs phenytoin monotherapy.
This is an observational epidemiological study describing the incidence of epilepsy over time. It is not a randomized controlled trial comparing any antiepileptic drugs.
This is a case series of 4 adults who developed absence seizures while on carbamazepine therapy. It is not a randomized controlled trial comparing carbamazepine vs phenytoin monotherapy.
This is an in vitro preclinical study examining drug effects on sodium channels in mammalian cell lines. It is not a clinical randomized controlled trial in humans.
This is an observational registry study describing the natural history and prevalence of epilepsy in Denmark. It is not a randomized controlled trial comparing antiepileptic drugs.

This is a counterbalanced, crossover double-blind study comparing carbamazepine with phenytoin in 40 adult epileptics. While the primary outcome focuses on psychotropic/cognitive effects rather than seizure control, this is a randomized controlled trial comparing the two drugs of interest in people with epilepsy. Conservative approach warrants inclusion.
This is a Cochrane review comparing phenobarbitone vs phenytoin, not carbamazepine vs phenytoin. The wrong intervention comparison for this review.
This is an observational record linkage study examining cutaneous reaction risks. It is not a randomized controlled trial comparing carbamazepine vs phenytoin monotherapy for seizure control.
This is a prospective community-based cohort study identifying prognostic factors for epilepsy remission. It is not a randomized controlled trial comparing antiepileptic drugs.

This is a randomized controlled trial comparing phenytoin (DPH) and carbamazepine (CBZ) in 40 newly diagnosed, drug-naive adult epileptic patients. Patients were randomized into DPH and CBZ groups. While the primary outcome is cognitive effects, this is a monotherapy comparison of the two drugs of interest in adults with epilepsy. Conservative approach warrants inclusion.

This is a randomized controlled trial comparing phenobarbital vs phenytoin, not carbamazepine vs phenytoin. The wrong intervention comparison for this review which specifically requires carbamazepine vs phenytoin.
This is a methodological paper about extracting statistics for meta-analysis of survival endpoints. It is not a primary randomized controlled trial comparing antiepileptic drugs.
